root_cause.text: handshake_req_cancel() in net/handshake failed to mark a request as completed when canceling a still-pending handshake removed from hn_requests, so a duplicate cancel could find the same request via handshake_rhashtbl and execute cancellation/refcount logic twice on the same socket.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states a canceled request is removed from handshake_net->hn_requests but remains in handshake_rhashtbl until destruction, causing a second cancel to see remove_pending() return false and proceed unless HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED is set; the patch fixes this by adding test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags) in the remove_pending(hn, req) path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Atomically mark removed pending handshake requests as completed during cancel and fail busy races instead of falsely reporting successful cancellation.
intent_record.what: In the branch where a pending handshake request is successfully removed via remove_pending(hn, req), the code replaces the old comment with one indicating cancellation and adds a test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags) check; if the bit was already set, it now calls trace_handshake_cancel_busy(net, req, sk) and returns false before falling through to the existing success path.
intent_record.how: This makes cancellation of a not-yet-accepted pending request atomically mark the request as completed/cancelled before reporting success, and it prevents reporting a successful cancel if another path already completed the request concurrently. At runtime, duplicate or racing cancellation/completion attempts are detected, traced, and rejected instead of being treated as a successful cancel.

grouping_result.intent: Atomically mark removed pending handshake requests as completed during cancel and fail busy races instead of falsely reporting successful cancellation.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by marking a pending handshake request as completed when it is removed during cancellation, preventing duplicate cancel operations from reprocessing the same request and correcting the race behavior.

candidates.rationale: This branch removes a still-pending request from the pending list but, before the fix, does not also mark the request completed. That leaves the request discoverable for a later duplicate cancel, enabling the cancellation/refcount path to run twice.

This early-success exit returns after removing the pending request without first setting the completed flag. That omission is the direct cause of falsely reporting successful cancellation while leaving the request eligible for duplicate cancellation handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early success exit is taken after a pending request is removed, but before the request is marked completed. That leaves the request still discoverable for a later duplicate cancel, allowing cancellation and refcount handling to run twice on the same socket.

This branch handles cancelation of a still-pending handshake by removing it from hn_requests, but in the pre-fix logic it does not also mark the request completed before succeeding. As a result, the same request can still be found again and canceled a second time.

net/handshake: Create a NETLINK service for handling handshake requests

When a kernel consumer needs a transport layer
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 3b3009ea8abb713b022d94fba95ec270cf6e7eae
Author: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>
Date:   Mon Apr 17 10:32:26 2023 -0400

    net/handshake: Create a NETLINK service for handling handshake requests
    
    When a kernel consumer needs a transport layer security session, it
    first needs a handshake to negotiate and establish a session. This
    negotiation can be done in user space via one of the several
    existing library implementations, or it can be done in the kernel.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of handshake_req_cancel(), which is enough to evaluate the root cause. In this version, after lookup (`req = handshake_req_hash_lookup(sk);`), the function checks whether the request is still pending: `if (hn && remove_pending(hn, req)) { /* Request hadn't been accepted */ goto out_true; }`. In that branch, it goes directly to `out_true` without setting `HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED`. Only the later non-pending path uses `if (test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags))` to mark completion / detect duplicates. Thus, canceling a still-pending request removes it from `hn_requests` but does not mark it completed. Because the request remains findable via `handshake_req_hash_lookup()` / `handshake_rhashtbl`, a duplicate cancel can find the same request again and run `sock_put(sk)` again. The fix is not present because there is no completed-bit marking before `goto out_true` in the pending-removal path.
